clue.text: Clown might start to break wild animal? What a nut!

parts.note: Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the animal's name, splitting it in two

parts.note: a deer is a wild animal

indicators.note: start of might means its opening letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A clown might set about smashing a wild beast, and the onlooker exclaims at the madness of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a nut!' reads as an exclamation about the clown; it is the definition, the coco de mer being the giant seed of a Seychelles palm.
explanation.definitionFit: The coco de mer is the enormous double coconut of a Seychelles palm, the largest seed in the plant kingdom.

clue.text: See 6 across
Discharge sailor in arch ploy

indicators.note: the sailor is placed in the middle of the reworked word
a ploy is a trick or manoeuvre, signalling that the letters of arch are rearranged

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is dismissed over some scheme involving an arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a verb about firing the sailor, but it is a noun: the mucus of a heavy cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is the excess mucus discharged from the nose and throat during a cold.

clue.text: In code it yields Hades, perhaps

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning code, it and yields

explanation.surface: A cipher reveals the underworld, as if decoding a secret message.
explanation.walkthrough: Hades is the Greek god of the underworld as well as the place, so 'perhaps' marks him as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades was a Greek god, ruler of the dead, so he is an example of a divine being.

clue.text: Stein's latest criminal picture?

parts.note: a stein is a beer mug, and the 's adds the S
hot news is the latest news

explanation.surface: Someone named Stein has made a new crime film or painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Stein reads as a surname; it is a beer mug, the possessive giving MUG'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A police photograph of an arrested suspect's face, taken for the records, is a criminal's picture.

clue.text: About to run race? She'll tell you all about it!

definitions.text: She'll tell you all about it

indicators.note: about here means turned around and moved, so the letters of the next three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner is about to compete, and a chatty friend will report the whole event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'nearly', but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller who relates anecdotes in an entertaining way.

clue.text: Act in your own best interests: perform singles with comics at fair

definitions.text: Act in your own best interests

parts.note: to play is to perform
ones are singles
cards are comical people, jokers
right means fair or just

explanation.surface: Advice to a performer: do solo numbers alongside the comedians at the funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comics' suggests comic books, but a card is a funny, eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: To play your cards right is an idiom for managing a situation shrewdly to gain advantage.

clue.text: Cover charge?

parts.note: not the fee for entering a club but the payment made for insurance cover

explanation.walkthrough: A cover charge is usually an entry fee at a nightclub; here the cover is insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance premium is the regular sum paid to keep a policy, the cost of being covered.

clue.text: Lush local choir improvised no end

indicators.note: something improvised is made up on the spot, so these letters are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of choir is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood choir sang off the cuff and seemingly without stopping, and the result was lush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' reads as an adjective praising the music; it is slang for a heavy drinker. 'no end' drops the R of choir, leaving CHOI to rearrange with LOCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush is slang for a drunkard, someone who habitually drinks too much.

clue.text: Horse racing establishment ultimately in decline

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of establishment

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken
rotting is declining, decaying

explanation.surface: A racing stable or course is said to be going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'establishment' looks like the racing business itself; only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotting is a form of harness racing in which horses pull sulkies at a trot.

clue.text: College poet's superior to church bully

parts.note: o'er is the poetic contraction of over, and over means superior
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A college poet looks down on the church and pushes it around.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce is to force someone by threats, which is what bullying does.

clue.text: Just what a smoker needs: Henry to go off the rails

indicators.note: the letter is to go, removed from the receptacle

parts.note: an ashtray is what a smoker wants to hand
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry, a smoker in need of a cigarette, is about to go off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person; it is the physics unit, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means wandering from the right path, so off the rails both literally and morally.

clue.text: Ladies do climax when holding nylon skirts!

indicators.note: the peak holds the outer letters inside it

parts.note: the height of something is its climax or peak

indicators.note: skirts means the edges or outskirts of nylon, its first and last letters

parts.note: the word whose edges are used

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a women's party reaching its peak as nylon skirts come into play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies do' is a noun, a party for women; 'skirts' is not clothing but the edges of the word nylon.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a party for a bride-to-be and her female friends before the wedding.

clue.text: Artist has to combat endless depression

parts.note: war is combat

indicators.note: the last letter of the hollow is cut off

parts.note: a hole is a depression in the ground

explanation.surface: A painter must fight off unending depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood, but it is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol was the American pop artist famous for soup cans and screen prints.

clue.text: Quiet spot, one in outskirts of Aachen, for a museum

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the German city whose edge letters are used
sh is a call for quiet
a mole is a spot on the skin
a means one

explanation.surface: Looking for a quiet place in the suburbs of Aachen to set up a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: Aachen tempts a German museum; the answer is in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean in Oxford is Britain's oldest public museum, of art and archaeology.

clue.text: Motel: it's about providing a recurring theme

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters of motel and it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
it, with the 's standing for 'is' as a link
if means providing, on condition that

explanation.surface: A motel claims to offer a recurring theme, perhaps in its décor or music.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurring musical phrase or idea tied to a character or situation, as in Wagner.

clue.text: Uncool underwear

parts.note: uncool suggests unfashionable, but it means literally not cool: warm undergarments

explanation.walkthrough: Uncool reads as unstylish; it is the literal sense, warm rather than cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermals are warm undergarments worn in cold weather, the opposite of cool clothing.

clue.text: Confess drinking wine is outrageous

indicators.note: the word for confessing takes in the wine as if drinking it

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
hock is German white wine

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to drinking wine, which is scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is British usage for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking means causing indignation or disgust, which is what something outrageous does.

clue.text: Notebooks where one enters criminal riches

indicators.note: the single letter goes into the rearranged word
criminal suggests something crooked, signalling the letters of riches are rearranged

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Notebooks recording where someone deposited ill-gotten wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cahiers is French for exercise books or notebooks, used in English for written records.

clue.text: Gang member's beastly sound overwhelming quiet

indicators.note: the growl surrounds and engulfs the word for quiet

parts.note: grr is the growl of an animal
ease is quiet, rest

explanation.surface: A gang member's animal growl drowns out the silence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'member's' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A greaser was a member of a youth gang of motorbike riders with slicked hair, in the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: Imperfect article on Jack — twisted etc

parts.note: re means on, about
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

indicators.note: twisted signals the letters of etc are rearranged

explanation.surface: A faulty piece about someone called Jack is a contorted mess and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a grammatical article or a news piece; with 'Imperfect' it is a flawed manufactured item.
explanation.definitionFit: A reject is a faulty manufactured product set aside as substandard.

clue.text: Stimulating sort of 8?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... one's memory is stimulating it
second meaning: a kind of 8 across, the gentle running pace

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 8 across, the slow pace a horse runs at; a slow human run is the same kind of thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Jogging is both prompting the memory and running at a steady slow pace, akin to a trot.

clue.text: Head back with close friend in America, showing easy good nature

indicators.note: back means the slang word for head is read in reverse

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
homie is US slang for a close friend

explanation.surface: Leaning back with a best mate in the States, everyone relaxed and genial.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful friendliness and geniality, an easy-going good-humoured manner.

clue.text: Barber upset oil initially on cloth provided

indicators.note: upset means the whole string is turned around
initially means the first letter of oil

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
a rag is a piece of cloth
if means provided

explanation.surface: A barber knocks over hair oil onto a towel, if that happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' sounds like the barber being cross; it reverses everything after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro is the barber of Seville in Beaumarchais's play and Rossini's opera.

clue.text: Admirers cherish grand feature of Dracula

definitions.note: singular in the clue, but the plural set of teeth is the feature

indicators.note: the admirers hold the letter close, as one holds something cherished

parts.note: fans are admirers
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Devotees treasure the grand look of Count Dracula.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula's long pointed canine teeth, used to bite victims, are his signature trait.

clue.text: See 6 across
Desert feed involved hollowed-out coconut

indicators.note: involved means tangled, signalling the letters of feed are rearranged
hollowed-out means the inside of coconut is removed, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: A desert island meal made from a scooped-out coconut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a sandy place; it is the verb to abandon a side.
explanation.definitionFit: To defect is to abandon one's country or cause for another, as a soldier deserts.

clue.text: US city in south, one that is protected by alien god

parts.note: an means one

indicators.note: the letters for that is sit inside the reworked word, shielded by it
alien means foreign, strange, signalling the letters of god are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the south, a figure is guarded by an extraterrestrial deity.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a major Californian city on the Pacific coast near Mexico.

clue.text: See 6
Vision of Barney nursing sore wound

indicators.note: the fight holds the reworked letters as one nurses a baby

parts.note: barney is British slang for a noisy quarrel or fight

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted, signals the letters of sore are rearranged

explanation.surface: A view of someone called Barney tending a painful injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Barney looks like a name, but in Britain a barney is a row. 'wound' is the past of wind, not an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is the ability to anticipate the future, a kind of vision.
